verified.entry_point: The User resource served by the manager: GET /user/{realm}/{userId}, GET /user/{realm}/userRoles/{userId}/{clientId}, GET /user/{realm}/userRealmRoles/{userId}, GET /user/{realm}/userSessions/{userId}, GET /user/{realm}/{clientId}/roles, GET /user/{realm}/disconnect/{sessionID}, GET /user/user, GET /user/userRoles/{clientId}, GET /user/userRealmRoles, PUT /user/locale
verified.project_tests_note: The project's own UserResourceTest is a Groovy integration test that starts the full manager against live Keycloak and PostgreSQL; it cannot run in the offline verifier. The hidden functional group drives the same resource operations with the same realm/user shape through the product's runtime classpath.

local.patch_matrix: each concept-missing patch fails only its own concept's security tests with all functional tests passing (miss-per-user 8, miss-role-definitions 3, miss-session-control 3 security failures); refuse-all leaves 16 functional errors, realm-equality 5 and current-user-header 1; crash-as-refusal, wrong-object and get-only leave 6-8 security failures and superuser-exempt 1; alternative and hardening score 1.0; the published fix leaves the three session-control tests failing (recall).

patch_checks.why: blind fix produced by run_blindfix after the first gate

wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the realm and user identifiers are used as given; there is no normalising, offset or conversion step on the attacker's value
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the identifiers are opaque strings with no parser whose spelling could hide the target from the guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the decision uses the realm and the identity directory; there is no separate authority that can return no role or secret
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the reference changes only the user-administration resource and one broker accessor; no sibling API's stated behaviour changes

traps.shape: The per-user profile read decides only on an administrative role or the caller's own identifier, while the user lookup is by identifier alone, so an own-realm path with a foreign user identifier returns that user.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the read consults only the administrative role and the caller's own identifier

traps.shape: The per-user client-role and realm-role lists carry the same administrative-role-or-own-identifier decision and pass the path realm into a realm-scoped lookup.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: same decision as the reported read, in the same file

traps.shape: The per-user session list is fetched from the broker by subject identifier only; the sink takes no realm.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the broker lookup filters on the subject identifier and nothing else

traps.shape: The realm-level client-role catalogue carries the read-admin annotation but never checks that the path realm is accessible, so the same decision is missing one level up from the per-user reads.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the route looks guarded by its role annotation and returns role definitions rather than user data

traps.shape: Session disconnection has no role annotation and no realm, ownership or role decision before it force-disconnects a broker connection by identifier.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the action takes only an opaque connection identifier and the sink is in another package

traps.shape: The current-user reads pass the client-supplied realm header into the per-user handlers, so a correct realm-and-user decision refuses the caller's own record when the header names another realm the caller administers.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code and the published fix moves these calls to the authenticated realm; an over-hardened per-user guard breaks them
